name: Sikafloor-324
paste:
SIKAFLOOR®-324: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sikafloor®-324, April 2023, Version 01.02 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/sikafloor_-324.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sikafloor®-324 where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02).
1.2 Product description.
    - Sikafloor®-324 is a two part solvent free, pigmented with FP3 epoxy paste, self smoothing polyurethane resin, with tough-elastic properties.
    - Sikafloor®-324 makes use of Sika's unique i-Cure technology to improve surface aesthetics and reduce sensitivity for ambient humidity during application.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer. Sikafloor®-324 may only be used by experienced professionals.
    - Car Park decks and ramps
    - Smooth wearing course with crack-bridging properties for industrial floors in production and storage facilities, work shops etc.
    - Broadcast wearing course with crack-bridging properties for wet working areas (food and beverage industry etc.),
    - Applicable on asphalt surfaces
    - Indoor areas, as in shopping centers, exhibition and storage areas.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.10.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sikafloor®-324
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 2-PART PUR TOUGH-ELASTIC, LOW-VOC, SELF SMOOTHING FLOOR
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Synthetic resin screed material according to EN 13813:2002, certified by Factory Production Control Body and provided with the CE-marking
    - Coating for concrete protection according to EN 1504-2:2004, certified by Factory Production Control Body and provided with the CE-marking
    - Fire classification according to DIN EN 13501-1:2010- 01: Report No. 20150909/01, MPA Dresden
    - Paint compatibility according to PV 3.10.7 tested at HQM Induserv Germany, test report 15-08- 15203573-001.
    - Crack bridging properties following to EN 1062-7 method A, Test report No: 51-15-0056, IBOS GmbH.
    - Slip resistance class determined according to DIN 51131, test reports 020109-15-16, 020109-15-16a, 020109-15-17, 020109-15-17a, 020109-15-18, 020109-15-18a
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - EN 13813:2002: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1504-2:2004: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN 13501-1:2010: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - EN 1062-7: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN 51131: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN ISO 2811-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Product Information > Density (p.2).
    - DIN 53505: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Shore D Hardness (p.2).
    - ASTM D 4060: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Abrasion resistance (p.2).
    - DIN EN ISO 527-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
    - ISO 527-2: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile strain at break (p.2).
    - EN 13892-8: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Tensile adhesion strength (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Flexible and tough-elastic
    - i-Cure based chemistry
    - Crack-bridging
    - Application on asphalt substrates possible (mastic asphalt)
    - Good chemical and mechanical resistance
    - Solvent-free and low VOC emissions
    - Possible slip resistant surface
    - Easy to apply and to keep clean
    - Economical
    - Not sensitive to moisture
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Polyurethane (PUR)
2.6 Appearance and colour.
    | Part A | coloured, liquid |
    | Part B | brownish, liquid |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
    Note printed: Sikafloor®-324 is available in broad range of colours.
2.7 Density.
    | Part A | ~1.4 kg/l |
    | Part B | ~1.2 kg/l |
    | Mixed resin (filled 1:0.5) | ~1.6 kg/l |
    Test method printed: (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    Note printed: Filling 1:0.5 with quartz sand F34 0.1–0.3 mm. All Density values at +23 °C.
2.8 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Solid content by mass: ~100 %
    - Solid content by volume: ~100 %
    - Shore D Hardness: ~ 60 (7 days/23 °C/50 % r.h.) (DIN 53505)
    - Abrasion resistance: ~ 65 mg (14 days/23 °C/50 % r.h.) (ASTM D 4060)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 14 N/mm2 (14 days/23 °C/50 % r.h.) (DIN EN ISO 527-2)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~ 90 % (resin / 28 days / +23 °C / 50 % r.h) (ISO 527-2)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: >1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (EN 13892-8)
    - Chemical resistance: Resistant to many chemicals. Contact Sika technical service for specific information.
2.9 Systems. Please refer to the System Data Sheet of:
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PS-32 | Smooth unicolour tough elastic poly- |
    | urethane floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PS-32 UV | Smooth unicolour tough elastic poly- |
    | urethane floor covering with UV sealer |
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PB-32 | Broadcast unicolour tough elastic |
    | polyurethane floor covering |
    | Sikafloor® MultiFlex PB-32 UV | Broadcast unicolour tough elastic |
    | polyurethane floor covering with UV sealer |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.10 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production
    - Storage conditions: The packaging must be stored properly in original, unopened and undamaged sealed packaging, in dry conditions at temperatures between +5 °C and +30 °C.
2.11 Packaging.
    | Part A | 20.25 kg containers |
    | Part B | 4.75 kg containers |
    | Part A+B | 25.0 kg ready to mix units |

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment. The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull of strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm². If in doubt apply a test area first.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 01.02) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Mixing ratio: Part A : Part B = 81 : 19 (by weight)
    - Consumption: Please refer to the System Data Sheets
4.3 Pot Life.
    | Temperatures | Time |
    | +10°C | ~ 40 minutes |
    | +20°C | ~ 30 minutes |
    | +30°C | ~ 20 minutes |
4.4 Curing time. Before overcoating Sikafloor®-324 allow:
    | Substrate temperature | Minimum | Maximum |
    | +10°C | ~ 30 hours | ~ 72 hours |
    | +20°C | ~ 24 hours | ~ 48 hours |
    | +30°C | ~ 16 hours | ~ 36 hours |
4.5 Applied product ready for use.
    | Temperature | Foot traffic | Light traffic | Full Cure |
    | +10°C | 1 day | 3 days | 9 days |
    | +20°C | 12 hours | 2 days | 5 days |
    | +30°C | 8 hours | 1 day | 3 days |
    Note printed: Note: Times are approximate and will be affected by changing ambient conditions
4.6 Mixing. Prior to mixing, stir part A mechanically. When all of part B has been added to part A mix continuously for 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. When parts A and B have been mixed, add the quartz sand F34 0.1–0.3 mm and mix for a further 2 minutes until a uniform mix has been achieved. To ensure thorough mixing pour the materials into another pail and mix again to achieve a consistent mix. After mixing leave the mixture for 3 minutes to react before applying.
4.7 Mixing - Mixing Tools. Sikafloor®-324 must be thoroughly mixed using a low speed electric stirrer (300 - 400 rpm) or other suitable equipment.
4.8 Application. Prior to application, confirm substrate moisture content, relative humidity and dew point. Sikafloor®-324 is poured and spread evenly by means of a serrated trowel or pin rake. When used in a selfsmoothing system, roll in two directions with a spike roller to ensure even thickness and to remove entrapped air.
4.9 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Thinner C immediately after use. Hardened and/or cured material can only be removed mechanically.
4.10 Limitations and important considerations.
    - Colour variations are un-avoidable due to raw materials. It can occur with quartz sand in bright shades such as yellow or orange where colour variations through the backfill may be visible. With these colours, the opacity is limited if the product is used as a top coat. Applying a reference area is strongly recommended.
    - Under UV and weathering changes in colour are possible. For colour matching, ensure Sikafloor®-324 components A and B are applied from the same control batch numbers.
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-324 on substrates with rising moisture.
    - Do not apply on substrate surfaces with a slope > 1 %.
    - Freshly applied Sikafloor®-324 must be protected from damp, condensation and water for at least 24 hours. Uncured material reacts in contact with water (foaming). During application care must be taken that no ‘sweat’ drops into fresh Sikafloor®-324 (wear head and wrist bands).
    - The incorrect assessment and treatment of cracks may lead to a reduced service life and reflective cracking.
    - In smooth applications with sun light exposure use Sikafloor®-357 N or Sikafloor®-305 W as seal coat.
    - Under certain conditions, under floor heating or high ambient temperatures combined with high point loading, may lead to imprints in the resin.
    - If during application temporary heating is required do not use gas, oil, paraffin or other fossil fuel heaters, these produce large quantities of both CO2 and H 2O water vapour, which may adversely affect the finish. For heating use only electric powered warm air blower systems.
4.11 Further information.
    - Substrate quality & Preparation
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “EVALUATION AND PREPARATION OF SURFACES FOR FLOORING SYSTEMS”.
    - Application instructions
    - Please refer to Sika Method Statement: “MIXING & APPLICATION OF FLOORING SYSTEMS”. Maintenance
    - Please refer to “Sikafloor®- CLEANING REGIME”.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.3 Relative air humidity. ~ 75–80 %
5.4 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3 °C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
5.5 Substrate temperature. +10 °C min. / +30 °C max.
5.6 Substrate moisture content. < 4 % pbw moisture content. Test method: Sika®-Tramex meter, CM - measurement or Oven-dry-method.No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
5.7 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.10):
    - Do not apply Sikafloor®-324 on substrates with rising moisture.
    - Under certain conditions, under floor heating or high ambient temperatures combined with high point loading, may lead to imprints in the resin.
5.8 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - The surface must be clean, dry and free of all contaminants such as dirt, oil, grease, coatings and surface treatments, etc. All dust, loose and friable material must be completely removed from all surfaces before application of the product, preferably by vacuum. Pull of strength shall not be less than 1.5 N/mm². If in doubt apply a test area first.
5.9 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Density: Part A | ~1.4 kg/l; Part B | ~1.2 kg/l; Mixed resin (filled 1:0.5) | ~1.6 kg/l (DIN EN ISO 2811-1)
    - Shore D Hardness: ~ 60 (7 days/23 °C/50 % r.h.) (DIN 53505)
    - Abrasion resistance: ~ 65 mg (14 days/23 °C/50 % r.h.) (ASTM D 4060)
    - Tensile strength: ~ 14 N/mm2 (14 days/23 °C/50 % r.h.) (DIN EN ISO 527-2)
    - Tensile strain at break: ~ 90 % (resin / 28 days / +23 °C / 50 % r.h) (ISO 527-2)
    - Tensile adhesion strength: >1.5 N/mm² (failure in concrete) (EN 13892-8)
5.10 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.11 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sikafloor®-324, April 2023, Version 01.02, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/g/sikafloor_-324.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikafloor 324 Part A, version 15/11/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/x/Sikafloor%20324%20Part%20A.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikafloor-324 Part B, version 19/03/2024, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/k/MSDS%20Sikafloor-324%20(B)%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS Sikafloor®-324 Part A, version 11/01/2026, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sds-sikafloor-324parta.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Ecology, health and safety - Directive 2004/42/ce limitation of emissions of.
    - VOC According to the EU-Directive 2004/42, the maximum allowed content of VOC (Product category IIA / j type sb) is 500 g/l (Limits 2010) for the ready to use product.
    - The maximum content of Sikafloor®-324 is < 500 g/l VOC for the ready to use product.
6.4 Maintenance - Cleaning. To maintain the appearance of the floor after application, Sikafloor®-324 must have all spillages removed immediately and be regularly cleaned using rotary brush, mechanical scrubbers, scrubber dryer, high pressure washer, wash and vacuum techniques etc., using suitable detergents and waxes.
6.5 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.6 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.7 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
